'''Anna Louise Lorck'''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/document/HansS_20201125_039660000/event|title=Event – New Zealand Parliament|website=www.parliament.nz}}</ref> is a New Zealand politician of the [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour Party]]. She served in the [[New Zealand House of Representatives]] as the MP for [[Tukituki (New Zealand electorate)|Tukituki]] from 2020 to 2023.<ref>{{Cite news |via=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |title=Election 2020: The 40 diverse new MPs entering Parliament |url= https://www.newstalkzb.co.nz/news/vote-2020/election-2020-the-forty-newcomers-entering-parliament/ |date=18 October 2020 |access-date=16 November 2020 |work=[[Newstalk ZB]] |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20201022040442/https://www.newstalkzb.co.nz/news/vote-2020/election-2020-the-forty-newcomers-entering-parliament/ |archive-date=22 October 2020}}</ref>

==Early life and career==
Lorck grew up in [[Waipukurau]] and trained as a journalist. Before entering parliament, she owned a public relations company.<ref name="HastingsMail2014">{{cite news|title=Lorck is Labour's latest candidate| work=Hastings Mail| first=Diane |last=Joyce|url= https://www.pressreader.com/new-zealand/the-hastings-mail/20140319/281530813966191|date=19 March 2014|access-date=19 March 2014}}</ref>

==Hawkes' Bay District Health Board==
Before standing as a Labour Party candidate, Lorck, who had vocally opposed Labour sacking the [[Hawke's Bay District Health Board]] (DHB), volunteered to phone canvass to motivate voter turnout for two hours for the [[New Zealand National Party|National Party]]. She was never a member of the party.<ref>{{cite news|url= http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11279732 |title=I'm no Nat, says Labour candidate Anna Lorck |work=[[Hawke's Bay Today]]|first=Harrison |last=Christian|date=23 June 2014|access-date=20 September 2017}}</ref>

In 2019 Lorck was elected to the Hawke's Bay DHB, as the highest polling new candidate.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.electionz.com/LGE2019Results/EL19DHB810_Results.pdf |title=Hawke's Bay District Health Board: 2019 Triennial Elections |publisher=[[Hawke's Bay District Health Board]] |last=Lampp |first=Warwick |date=18 October 2019 |access-date=19 October 2020 }}</ref> She served as part of the governance of the region's response to COVID-19. Lorck advocates for a local cardiology centre, costed at $15 million, to enable life-saving surgery locally.<ref name="third-time lucky"/>

==Political career==
===Labour parliamentary candidate, 2014–2020===

At the {{NZ election link year|2014}} election, Lorck, a Hastings business woman, stood as a candidate in the {{NZ electorate link|Tukituki}} electorate for the Labour Party, and did not stand on the Labour list. As a first time candidate she made significant progress into the margin against incumbent [[New Zealand National Party|National Party]] MP [[Craig Foss]], and  announced she would stand again at the {{NZ election link year|2017}} election. She was ranked 46 on the Labour party list.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 August 2017 |title=Revised Labour Party List for the 2017 Election |url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO1708/S00314/revised-labour-party-list-for-the-2017-election.htm |publisher=[[Scoop (website)|Scoop]] |access-date=15 August 2017 }}</ref>

During a tightly fought contest, in July 2017 a complaint by a right-wing blogger, was made against Lorck to the Advertising Standards Authority over her billboard wording of "Your Local MP". Lorck responded by stating the intention of the message was to convey that she lived in the Tukituki electorate while National candidate [[Lawrence Yule]] lived in neighboring Napier.<ref>{{cite news |url= https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/95099736/complaints-made-over-billboard-that-appears-to-say-candidate-is-local-mp-when-she-is-not |title=Complaints made over billboard that appears to say candidate is local MP when she is not | work=[[Hawke's Bay Today]] |author=Sharpe, Marty |date=25 July 2017 |access-date=20 September 2017 }}</ref> Lorck again made significant inroads into the majority but was not elected, nor ranked high enough on the Labour list to be elected to Parliament.<ref name="third-time lucky">{{cite news|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/300119313/election-2020-can-labours-anna-lorck-make-it-thirdtime-lucky-in-tukituki |title=Can Labour's Anna Lorck make it 'third-time lucky' in Tukituki? |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |author=Sharpe, Marty |date=7 October 2020 |access-date=19 October 2020 }}</ref>

At the [[2020 New Zealand general election|2020 general election]], Lorck was selected as the Labour candidate for Tukituki for the third time. She was given the Labour Party's endorsement to run a local MP campaign and consequently was not on the [[party list]].<ref name="third-time lucky"/> This time she unseated Yule by a margin of 1590 votes, returning the electorate to Labour for the first time since 2002.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tukituki – Official Result |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/electorate-details-54.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=7 January 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/123125236/election-2020-nationals-lawrence-yule-on-being-ousted-in-tukituki-after-20-years-in-hawkes-bay-politics |title=National's Lawrence Yule on being ousted in Tukituki after 20 years in Hawke's Bay politics |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |author=Gilbertson, Georgia-May |date=18 October 2020 |access-date=19 October 2020 }}</ref>

===Member of Parliament===
In August 2022, a former senior staffer within the [[New Zealand Parliament]] alleged that Lorck had bullied her, and that Lorck had been through three executive assistants in a year and a half.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Witton |first=Bridie |date=12 August 2022 |title=Senior staffer levels bullying allegation at Labour MP |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/129559320/senior-staffer-levels-bullying-allegation-at-labour-mp |access-date=12 August 2022 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220902035040/https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/123125236/election-2020-nationals-lawrence-yule-on-being-ousted-in-tukituki-after-20-years-in-hawkes-bay-politics|archive-date=2 September 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> In September 2022, a second former staffer made allegations of bullying including "persistent scolding" against Lorck. In response to media coverage, Lorck confirmed that she was undergoing leadership training and claimed that she had never received complaints of bullying from the staffer during their employment period.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Witton |first1=Bridie |title=Fresh bullying allegations against Labour MP Anna Lorck. MP says she's working with a leadership coach |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/129827684/fresh-bullying-allegations-against-labour-mp-anna-lorck-mp-says-shes-working-with-a-leadership-coach |access-date=19 September 2022 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=15 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220915012720/https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/129827684/fresh-bullying-allegations-against-labour-mp-anna-lorck-mp-says-shes-working-with-a-leadership-coach |archive-date=15 September 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Labour MP Anna Lorck in leadership training after bullying accusations |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/474810/labour-mp-anna-lorck-in-leadership-training-after-bullying-accusations |access-date=19 September 2022 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=15 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220915042836/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/474810/labour-mp-anna-lorck-in-leadership-training-after-bullying-accusations |archive-date=15 September 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>

During the [[2023 New Zealand general election]], Lorck was [[Unseating|unseated]] by National Party candidate [[Catherine Wedd]], who won by a margin of 10,118 votes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tukituki - Official Result |url=https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-54.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=18 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231123104119/https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-54.html |archive-date=23 November 2023 |date=3 November 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Hawke’s Bay Power Consumers Trust ===
In 2024, Lorck stood for election to the Hawke's Bay Power Consumers Trust Board but was not elected, receiving the fewest votes among the candidates.<ref>{{cite news |title=Hawke's Bay Power Consumers Trust election: Four out of five trustees retain their seat |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/hawkes-bay-today/news/hawkes-bay-power-consumers-trust-election-four-out-of-five-trustees-retain-their-seat/4US7GZYFLFBCRCCSPU65YK6SOM/ |access-date=21 January 2025 |work=[[Hawke's Bay Today]] |agency=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=2 October 2024}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Lorck is married to former [[Hastings District Council|Hastings District Councillor]] Damon Harvey.<ref>{{Cite press release |last1=Harvey |last2=Lorck |first2=Anna |first1=Damon |title=Decision of BSA and announcement of defamation proceedings |agency=[[Scoop (website)|Scoop]] |url= https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/AK1808/S00622/decision-of-bsa-and-announcement-of-defamation-proceedings.htm |access-date=27 October 2020 |date=27 August 2018}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite news |title=Local Focus: MP Anna Lorck ends husband Damon Harvey's political ambition|url= https://www.nzherald.co.nz/hawkes-bay-today/news/local-focus-mp-anna-lorck-ends-husband-damon-harveys-political-ambition/HFP3IF2QF4KNZFU3PQY32RSOGY/ |access-date=27 October 2020| work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] }}</ref> They have a blended family of five children.<ref name=":0" />
